label: Step 1
text: Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.

label: Step 2
text: Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken until browned on both sides and cooked through. Move it to a plate.

label: Step 3
text: Lower the heat. Add the sliced garlic and cook for one minute without letting it brown.

label: Step 4
text: Add the spinach and the juice of the lemon. Stir until the spinach wilts. Return the chicken and spoon the pan sauce over it.

label: Tip
text: While the chicken sears, slice the garlic and squeeze the lemon for steps 3 and 4.

label: FAQ: chicken too dry
text: Slice the breast in half horizontally so it cooks faster and stays juicy. Thighs also work and are harder to overcook.

label: FAQ: no lemon
text: A splash of white wine vinegar gives the sauce acidity. Bottled lemon juice works but tastes flatter.

label: FAQ: sticking pan
text: Leave it a minute longer. Once the underside browns it releases on its own; forcing it tears the crust.

label: Step 1
text: Heat the oven to 200 C (400 F). Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt, the milk if using, and the grated parmesan.

label: Step 2
text: Melt the butter in an oven-safe skillet and soften the sliced onion for five minutes. Add the spinach and stir until it wilts.

label: Step 3
text: Pour in the eggs and cook without stirring until the edges set. Move the skillet to the oven and bake until the center is set.

label: Tip
text: While the onion softens, whisk the eggs with the parmesan so step 3 is ready to pour.

label: FAQ: no oven-safe skillet
text: Cook it covered on the stove over low heat until the top sets. The top will not brown.

label: FAQ: no milk
text: Leave it out or use a splash of water. Milk makes the frittata a little softer but is not needed.

label: FAQ: frozen spinach
text: Thaw it and squeeze out as much water as you can first, or the frittata turns watery.

label: Step 1
text: Scramble the eggs in a hot oiled skillet until just set and move them to a plate.

label: Step 2
text: Add the cold cooked rice, the diced carrot and the peas. Spread the rice out and let it fry without stirring for a minute before tossing.

label: Step 3
text: Add the soy sauce and the eggs back in. Toss and finish with sliced scallions and a few drops of sesame oil.

label: Tip
text: Slice the scallions before you start: once the rice hits the pan everything moves fast.

label: FAQ: freshly cooked rice
text: Fresh rice turns mushy. Spread it on a plate and chill it for 20 minutes first.

label: FAQ: no wok
text: A wide skillet works. Cook in two batches so the rice fries instead of steaming.

label: FAQ: no sesame oil
text: Skip it. It adds aroma at the end but the dish works without it. Do not fry with it: it burns at high heat.

label: Step 1
text: Rinse the rice and start cooking it with about 1 1/2 times its volume of water.

label: Step 2
text: Cut the chicken thighs into bite-size pieces. Grate the ginger and mince the garlic. Stir the soy sauce and honey together in a small bowl.

label: Step 3
text: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken in one layer and cook until browned and cooked through, turning once.

label: Step 4
text: Add the green beans and a splash of water. Cover and cook until the beans are bright green and just tender.

label: Step 5
text: Add the ginger and garlic, stir for 30 seconds, then pour in the soy-honey sauce. Toss until the sauce is glossy and coats everything. Serve over the rice.

label: Tip
text: While the chicken browns, trim the green beans so they are ready for step 4.

label: FAQ: chicken breast instead of thighs
text: Breast works. Cut it a little thicker and take it off the heat as soon as it is cooked through, because it dries out faster than thighs.

label: FAQ: no fresh ginger
text: Leave it out rather than using ground ginger in large amounts; a small pinch of ground ginger is fine but it tastes different.

label: FAQ: sauce burns
text: Honey burns quickly. Lower the heat before adding the sauce and keep tossing; add a spoon of water if it gets too thick.

label: Step 1
text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until just tender. Add the frozen peas for the last two minutes.

label: Step 2
text: Before draining, scoop out a cup of the pasta water. Drain the pasta and peas.

label: Step 3
text: Melt the butter in the empty pot or a skillet over low heat. Add the sliced garlic and cook gently until fragrant but not brown.

label: Step 4
text: Add the pasta, peas, parmesan and a splash of pasta water. Toss until a light sauce forms. Finish with lemon zest and a squeeze of juice if using.

label: Tip
text: While the water heats, slice the garlic and grate the lemon zest.

label: FAQ: sauce is dry or clumpy
text: Add more pasta water a spoonful at a time and keep tossing off the heat. The starch in the water makes the cheese smooth.

label: FAQ: no parmesan
text: Any hard grated cheese works. Without cheese, add a little more butter and salt; it will be lighter.

label: FAQ: olive oil instead of butter
text: Olive oil works for a lighter version. The sauce will be less creamy.

label: Step 1
text: Start the rice. Cut the tomatoes into wedges and slice the scallions. Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt.

label: Step 2
text: Heat half the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in the eggs, stir gently until softly set, and move them to a plate.

label: Step 3
text: Add the rest of the oil and the tomatoes. Cook, stirring, until they soften and release their juice.

label: Step 4
text: Stir in the sugar and the soy sauce if using. Return the eggs, fold them in, and finish with scallions. Serve over rice.

label: Tip
text: While the tomatoes cook, check the rice so both are ready together.

label: FAQ: why sugar
text: A little sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes. Reduce it if your tomatoes are very sweet, but do not skip it entirely.

label: FAQ: too watery
text: Cook the tomatoes a minute longer before adding the eggs back, so some of the juice cooks off.

label: FAQ: canned tomatoes
text: Diced canned tomatoes work in a pinch. Drain them first; the texture will be softer.

label: Step 1
text: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until just tender. Save half a cup of pasta water, then drain.

label: Step 2
text: Meanwhile heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sliced mushrooms and cook without stirring until browned, then stir and cook until their liquid is gone.

label: Step 3
text: Add the minced garlic for 30 seconds, then the marinara. Simmer for five minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, if using.

label: Step 4
text: Toss the pasta with the sauce and a splash of pasta water. Top with parmesan if using.

label: Tip
text: Slice the mushrooms while the water comes to a boil.

label: FAQ: mushrooms are soggy
text: Use a hot pan and do not crowd it. Cook them in two batches if needed and salt them only after they brown.

label: FAQ: no mushrooms
text: Zucchini cut into half-moons works the same way. Without vegetables it becomes a plain marinara pasta.

label: FAQ: vegan
text: Skip the parmesan. The rest of the recipe has no animal products.

label: Step 1
text: Start the rice. Slice the chicken, peppers and onion into thin strips.

label: Step 2
text: Toss the chicken with half the smoked paprika and a pinch of salt. Heat half the oil in a skillet and cook the chicken until browned and cooked through. Move it to a plate.

label: Step 3
text: Add the rest of the oil, the peppers and the onion with the remaining paprika. Cook until soft and charred at the edges.

label: Step 4
text: Warm the drained black beans in the same pan for two minutes.

label: Step 5
text: Build bowls with rice, beans, chicken and vegetables. Top with pico de gallo and sliced avocado if using.

label: Tip
text: While the chicken cooks, drain and rinse the beans.

label: FAQ: no smoked paprika
text: Regular paprika with a pinch of chili powder works. It will be less smoky.

label: FAQ: make it vegetarian
text: Leave out the chicken and use a second can of beans. Cook the vegetables the same way.

label: FAQ: tortillas instead of rice
text: Warm flour tortillas and serve the filling as fajitas. You can skip the rice entirely.

label: Step 1
text: Dice the onion. Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and add the ground beef and onion. Break the meat up as it browns.

label: Step 2
text: Stir in the smoked paprika and a pinch of salt with two tablespoons of water. Cook until the beef is fully cooked and the pan is almost dry.

label: Step 3
text: Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for about 20 seconds per side.

label: Step 4
text: Fill the tortillas with beef, cheddar and pico de gallo. Add sliced avocado if using.

label: Tip
text: While the beef browns, warm the tortillas in a second pan so everything is ready at once.

label: FAQ: no beef
text: Ground chicken or turkey works the same way. Add a little oil because they are leaner.

label: FAQ: too greasy
text: Spoon off the extra fat after the beef browns and before you add the paprika.

label: FAQ: corn tortillas
text: Corn tortillas work. Warm them well or they crack; doubling them up helps.

label: Step 1
text: Start the rice. Mince the garlic and stir it with the honey and soy sauce.

label: Step 2
text: Pat the salmon dry and season lightly with salt. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and cook the salmon skin side down until crisp.

label: Step 3
text: Flip the salmon and cook until it flakes easily, then move it to a plate.

label: Step 4
text: Add the green beans and a splash of water, cover and steam until just tender.

label: Step 5
text: Lower the heat, pour in the honey-garlic sauce and let it bubble for 30 seconds. Return the salmon, spoon the sauce over and serve with the rice and beans.

label: Tip
text: While the salmon cooks, trim the green beans for step 4.

label: FAQ: skinless salmon
text: Skinless works. Cook it a little shorter on the first side and handle it gently when flipping.

label: FAQ: frozen salmon
text: Thaw it in the fridge overnight and pat it very dry before cooking, or it will steam instead of browning.

label: FAQ: sauce burns
text: Take the pan off the heat before adding the sauce if it is very hot. Honey and garlic burn in seconds.

label: Step 1
text: Cut the potatoes into small cubes, the zucchini into half-moons and the onion into dice.

label: Step 2
text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the potatoes with a pinch of salt, cover and cook, stirring now and then, until tender and golden.

label: Step 3
text: Add the onion, zucchini and smoked paprika. Cook uncovered until the vegetables are soft.

label: Step 4
text: Make four wells in the hash and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook until the whites are set. Sprinkle with cheddar if using.

label: Tip
text: While the potatoes cook, cut the zucchini and onion for step 3.

label: FAQ: potatoes still hard
text: Keep the lid on and lower the heat slightly; add a spoon of water if they start to stick. Small cubes cook much faster.

label: FAQ: no zucchini
text: Bell pepper, mushrooms or spinach all work. Add spinach at the very end so it just wilts.

label: FAQ: make ahead
text: Cook the potato hash ahead and reheat it, then add the eggs fresh. The eggs do not reheat well.

label: Step 1
text: Start the rice. Dice the onion, mince the garlic and grate the ginger.

label: Step 2
text: Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and soften the onion. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for one minute.

label: Step 3
text: Add the drained chickpeas, coconut milk and curry sauce. Simmer until slightly thickened.

label: Step 4
text: Stir in the kale, stems removed and leaves torn, and cook until tender. Taste for salt and serve over rice.

label: Tip
text: While the curry simmers, strip the kale leaves from their stems.

label: FAQ: too spicy
text: Add more coconut milk or a squeeze of lemon. Serving with extra rice also helps.

label: FAQ: spinach instead of kale
text: Spinach works. Add it at the very end; it wilts in under a minute.

label: FAQ: no curry sauce
text: Use about two teaspoons of curry powder fried with the onion and add a little salt. The flavor will be simpler.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: Chicken is done when the thickest part reaches 165 F (74 C) on a thermometer and the juices run clear. With no thermometer, cut into the thickest piece: it should be white all the way through.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use thin-sliced chicken breast, or slice each breast in half horizontally; it cooks in about 3 minutes per side. Pre-washed spinach saves another few minutes.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Take the chicken off the heat as soon as it reaches 165 F and let it rest on the plate for 2 minutes; the pan sauce in step 4 adds moisture back.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: It is done when the center no longer jiggles and a knife in the middle comes out clean, about 12 minutes in the oven. The eggs should be fully set (160 F / 71 C).

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Butter the whole pan, including the sides, and let the edges set before you move anything. Run a spatula around the edge before sliding it out.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Skip the oven: cover the pan and cook on low heat until the top sets, about 8 minutes. Slice the onion thin so it softens faster.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Take it out as soon as the center is just set; it keeps cooking from the pan's heat. Overbaked eggs turn rubbery and weep water.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Heat the pan and oil until shimmering before the rice goes in, and do not stir for the first minute. A nonstick skillet helps; add a little more oil if it still sticks.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: It is ready when the rice is hot all the way through, some grains are lightly toasted, and the eggs are fully set.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use rice cooked yesterday or a microwave rice pouch, and frozen peas so the only chopping is the scallions.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy and moist
text: If it tastes dry, add a tablespoon of water mixed into the soy sauce at the end rather than more oil.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: The chicken is done at 165 F (74 C) in the thickest piece, with no pink inside and clear juices.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Pat the chicken dry, let the pan get hot before adding it, and do not move the pieces until they brown; they release on their own.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use a microwave rice pouch and frozen cut green beans, and buy chicken already cut for stir-fry.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Thighs stay juicy; cook them in one layer so they brown instead of steaming, and stop as soon as they reach 165 F.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: Pasta is done when it is tender but still slightly firm in the center (al dente). Taste a strand a minute before the package time.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Use a big pot of boiling salted water and stir during the first minute. Toss the pasta with the butter right after draining.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Thin spaghetti or angel hair cooks in a few minutes, and a lid on the pot brings the water to a boil faster.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy and saucy
text: Keep a little extra pasta water and add a splash just before serving; the sauce thickens as it cools.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: The eggs are cooked through but still soft, and the tomatoes have softened into a glossy sauce.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Let the oil get hot before the eggs go in and keep them moving gently; a nonstick pan makes this easy.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Cut the tomatoes while the rice cooks, or use a microwave rice pouch. The stir-fry itself takes about 5 minutes.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Take the eggs off while still soft and glossy; they finish in the sauce. Cover the pan for a minute so the tomatoes release more juice.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: The pasta is al dente (tender with a slight bite) and the sauce has simmered until it clings to a spoon.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Stir the pasta in its first minute of boiling, and toss it with the sauce right after draining.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Buy pre-sliced mushrooms and start the sauce while the water comes to a boil.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy and saucy
text: Add a splash of pasta water when tossing; it loosens the sauce and helps it coat the spaghetti.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: The chicken strips are done at 165 F (74 C), white throughout with no pink.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Pat the chicken dry, heat the oil first, and let the strips brown before turning them.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use pre-sliced peppers and onions and a microwave rice pouch; the cooking itself takes about 12 minutes.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Slice the chicken thin so it cooks fast, take it off as soon as it is done, and let it rest while the vegetables cook.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: Ground beef is done at 160 F (71 C), with no pink left.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Let the beef brown before breaking it up; the browned bits lift off when you add the two tablespoons of water in step 2.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Warm the tortillas in the microwave under a damp paper towel for 30 seconds instead of in a pan.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Keep a spoon of the cooking liquid with the beef and add the pico de gallo just before eating.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: Salmon is done at 145 F (63 C), when it turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Pat the fish dry, heat the oil until it shimmers, and leave the skin side down until it releases on its own.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Cut the salmon into cubes so it cooks in about 4 minutes, and use a microwave rice pouch.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Take the salmon off as soon as it flakes; it keeps cooking for a minute on the plate.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: The potatoes are done when a fork slides in easily and the edges are golden. The egg whites should be fully set; cook 2 more minutes for firm yolks.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Use enough oil to coat the pan, and stir only every few minutes so a crust forms and lets go.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Microwave the potato cubes for 4 minutes before they go in the pan; they only need to brown.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Keep the lid on while the potatoes cook and add the zucchini later so it stays tender, not dry.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: It is ready when the sauce has thickened a little and the kale is tender.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Stir from the bottom now and then and keep the heat at a gentle simmer; add a splash of water if it catches.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use a microwave rice pouch and simmer for just 5 minutes; the canned chickpeas only need to heat through.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy and creamy
text: If it gets too thick, stir in a little more coconut milk or water.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: Step 1
text: Start the rice. Slice the onion thinly and cut the chicken into bite-size pieces.

label: Step 2
text: Simmer the onion with the soy sauce, sugar and 120 ml (1/2 cup) of water in a small skillet until soft.

label: Step 3
text: Add the chicken in one layer, cover and simmer until cooked through, turning once.

label: Step 4
text: Beat the eggs lightly and pour them over in a circle. Cover and cook until the eggs are just set, then slide everything over bowls of rice and top with scallions.

label: Tip
text: While the onion simmers, beat the eggs in a bowl so step 4 is ready to pour.

label: FAQ: no dashi
text: This version uses water with soy sauce and sugar. If you have dashi, use it instead of water for a deeper flavor.

label: FAQ: runny eggs
text: Traditional oyakodon keeps the eggs soft. For fully set eggs, keep the lid on a minute longer.

label: FAQ: chicken breast instead
text: Breast works; slice it thin and take it off the heat as soon as it is cooked through so it stays tender.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: The chicken is done at 165 F (74 C) with no pink inside; the eggs are done when they are set to your liking.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Keep enough simmering liquid in the pan; add a splash of water if it gets low.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use a microwave rice pouch and cut the chicken small so it cooks in about 5 minutes.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Thighs stay juicy; simmer gently with the lid on rather than boiling hard.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: Step 1
text: Start the rice. Beat the eggs with the sugar and half the soy sauce until smooth.

label: Step 2
text: Wilt the spinach in a dry pan, squeeze out the water, and toss it with the sesame oil and the rest of the soy sauce.

label: Step 3
text: Oil the skillet lightly over medium-low heat. Pour in a thin layer of egg; when it is almost set, roll it to one side. Repeat with the rest of the egg, rolling each layer around the last.

label: Step 4
text: Rest the omelette for a minute, slice it, and serve with the spinach and rice.

label: Tip
text: While the rice cooks, wash the spinach so step 2 is quick.

label: FAQ: no square pan
text: A small round skillet works. Fold the edges in to keep a log shape; the ends will just be rounder.

label: FAQ: omelette tearing
text: Lower the heat and wait until the top is almost set before rolling; a little more oil helps too.

label: FAQ: less sweet
text: Halve the sugar or leave it out for a savory version, then add a pinch of salt.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: Each layer should be set but still soft; the rolled omelette is done when no liquid egg runs out when you slice it (eggs cooked to 160 F / 71 C).

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Wipe the pan with a little oil before every layer and keep the heat medium-low.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Skip the rolling: cook it as a soft scramble with the same seasoning. Use a microwave rice pouch.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Low heat keeps the layers tender and moist; high heat makes them tough and dry.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: Step 1
text: Start the rice. Cut the chicken, potato, carrot and onion into bite-size pieces.

label: Step 2
text: Heat the oil in a pot and brown the chicken and onion.

label: Step 3
text: Add the potato, carrot, curry sauce, coconut milk and 120 ml (1/2 cup) of water. Cover and simmer until the potato is tender.

label: Step 4
text: Taste for salt and serve over the rice.

label: Tip
text: While the curry simmers, set the table; it needs only an occasional stir.

label: FAQ: curry roux blocks
text: If you have Japanese curry roux, use 2 blocks instead of the curry sauce and coconut milk, and add water as the box says.

label: FAQ: too spicy
text: Add more coconut milk or a little honey to soften the heat.

label: FAQ: vegetarian
text: Leave out the chicken and add a can of drained chickpeas with the potatoes.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: It is done when the potato is fork-tender and the chicken reaches 165 F (74 C).

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Stir from the bottom every few minutes and keep it at a gentle simmer; add a splash of water if it thickens too much.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Cut the potato and carrot small so they cook in about 10 minutes, and use a microwave rice pouch.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy and saucy
text: Simmer with the lid on so the sauce does not reduce too far; add water if it gets thick.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out. Curry often tastes even better the next day.

label: Step 1
text: Drain the beans and mash them lightly with a fork. Dice the pepper.

label: Step 2
text: Spread beans on half of each tortilla, add pepper and cheese, and fold.

label: Step 3
text: Cook in a dry skillet over medium heat until golden on both sides and the cheese melts.

label: Step 4
text: Cut into wedges and serve with pico de gallo and avocado.

label: Tip
text: While the first batch cooks, slice the avocado.

label: FAQ: no cheddar
text: Any melting cheese works, such as mozzarella or pepper jack.

label: FAQ: falling apart
text: Mash the beans so they hold together, and do not overfill; press the quesadilla gently with the spatula.

label: FAQ: add meat
text: Leftover chicken from another recipe is a good add; warm it first.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: It is done when both sides are golden and crisp and the cheese has melted.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Use a dry or very lightly oiled skillet over medium heat and flip once the bottom is golden.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Cook two at once in a big skillet, or melt them in the microwave for a softer version.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Add a spoon of pico de gallo inside so the filling stays moist.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: Step 1
text: Boil salted water and cook the spaghetti until al dente. Save half a cup of pasta water.

label: Step 2
text: Melt the butter in a skillet and brown the chicken pieces until cooked through. Move them to a plate.

label: Step 3
text: Brown the mushrooms in the same pan, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the milk. Simmer until slightly thickened.

label: Step 4
text: Stir in the parmesan, then the pasta and chicken, adding pasta water until creamy.

label: Tip
text: While the chicken browns, slice the mushrooms and mince the garlic.

label: FAQ: sauce too thin
text: Simmer a minute longer, or add a little more parmesan; it thickens as it cools.

label: FAQ: sauce split
text: Keep the heat low after adding milk and do not let it boil hard.

label: FAQ: no chicken
text: Leave it out and add more mushrooms or a can of chickpeas.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: The chicken is done at 165 F (74 C); the pasta is tender with a slight bite.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Stir the pasta in its first minute, and do not move the chicken until it browns and releases.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use pre-sliced mushrooms and cook the chicken while the water boils.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy and creamy
text: Take the chicken off as soon as it is done and add pasta water at the end for a silky sauce.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: Step 1
text: Cook the spaghetti until just tender, then drain.

label: Step 2
text: Stir the soy sauce, sesame oil and honey together in a bowl.

label: Step 3
text: Stir-fry the carrot and zucchini in a hot pan for 2 minutes so they stay crisp.

label: Step 4
text: Toss in the noodles and sauce, and top with scallions and a fried egg if you like.

label: Tip
text: While the noodles boil, cut the vegetables into thin sticks.

label: FAQ: real noodles
text: Ramen or udon noodles work in place of spaghetti; cook them as the package says.

label: FAQ: too salty
text: Add a squeeze of lemon or a little more honey and a splash of water.

label: FAQ: eat cold
text: It is good cold too; toss with the sauce and chill for 20 minutes.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: It is ready when the noodles are tender and the vegetables are hot but still a little crisp.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Rinse the cooked noodles briefly or toss them with a drop of sesame oil so they do not clump.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use a bag of pre-cut vegetables and boil the water with a lid on.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy and saucy
text: Save a spoon of noodle water and toss it in with the sauce.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: Step 1
text: Soften the onion and pepper in the olive oil.

label: Step 2
text: Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds, then the marinara. Simmer until slightly thick.

label: Step 3
text: Make four wells and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook until the whites are set.

label: Step 4
text: Top with parmesan if you like and serve straight from the pan.

label: Tip
text: While the vegetables soften, crack the eggs into a cup so step 3 is quick.

label: FAQ: no bread
text: Serve it over rice or with tortillas warmed in a dry pan.

label: FAQ: too spicy
text: Smoked paprika is mild; for less smoky flavor use half.

label: FAQ: firm yolks
text: Keep the lid on 2 to 3 minutes longer.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: It is done when the egg whites are fully set; cook longer for firm yolks (160 F / 71 C).

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer and stir before adding the eggs.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Skip the pepper and simmer the sauce for just 2 minutes before adding the eggs.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Add a splash of water if the sauce thickens too much before the eggs are done.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.

label: Step 1
text: Start the rice. Trim and cut the green beans, grate the ginger and mince the garlic.

label: Step 2
text: Cook the green beans in the oil until blistered in spots. Move them to a plate.

label: Step 3
text: Brown the beef, breaking it up, until no pink remains. Add the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds.

label: Step 4
text: Stir in the soy sauce and honey, return the beans, and serve over the rice.

label: Tip
text: While the beans cook, mix the soy sauce and honey in a cup.

label: FAQ: no beef
text: Ground chicken or turkey works the same way; add a little more oil.

label: FAQ: too greasy
text: Spoon off extra fat after browning the beef, before adding the sauce.

label: FAQ: frozen green beans
text: They work; cook them a little longer and pat them dry first.

label: FAQ: is it done
text: Ground beef is done at 160 F (71 C) with no pink left.

label: FAQ: sticking
text: Let the beef brown before breaking it up; a splash of water lifts the browned bits.

label: FAQ: short on time
text: Use frozen cut green beans and a microwave rice pouch.

label: FAQ: keep it juicy
text: Do not cook the beef dry; add the sauce as soon as the pink is gone.

label: FAQ: leftovers
text: Cool it and refrigerate within 2 hours; eat within 3 to 4 days (USDA FoodKeeper, leftovers). Reheat until steaming hot, with a splash of water so it does not dry out.
